audit_kind: Read-only development-source state-machine audit; not released-artifact qualification
count_semantics: Machine families are analytical ownership groupings. Transition rows describe observed branches/temporal protocols; counts are not product feature counts or proof of formal exhaustiveness.

recommendation.decision: Adopt one explicit transition contract per subsystem owner, with a shared vocabulary for outcomes and effects, and derive capabilities, diagnostics, workflow guidance and conformance checks from those owned contracts.
recommendation.scope: An incremental internal architecture decision. Preserve host-specific behavior and the existing native transaction kernel. No repository changes were made by this audit.
axes: pending, active, review, completed, blocked, retired
A user or agent can update progress without manufacturing verification or authorization.
absent, current, stale, contradicted, partial, unavailable
A result names the source revision, scope and producer; stale proof does not silently rewrite historical progress.
unestablished, granted for exact scope, denied, revoked or expired
A transition description is not an authority grant. Existing explicit user and host constraints remain controlling.
not requested, intent recorded, attempted, observed, outcome unknown
Committed local state and successfully delivered external effect are different facts. Unknown outcomes require observation before retry.
queued, running, cancel requested, quiescent, cleanup failed
A process exit, timeout request or closed UI is not proof all writers/resources stopped.
subject revision, input digest, operation id, owner/session/epoch

Callbacks and retries must remain bound to the exact operation and owner. Cancellation/disposal invalidates stale UI updates and ordinary execution authority; explicitly owned cleanup and outcome reconciliation remain permitted until settled.
fields: effect intents and their owning executor
preserve: Keep existing stable IDs, schema/wire fields, operation-id replay, before-image history, canonical serialization and registered file ownership.
Keep ordinary progress assistive. A missing optional attestation must not become a new permission ceremony or universal blocker.
Preserve actual hard stops, explicit authority and host capability limits. Do not repair Pi child authors by bypassing unavailable confirmation or audit controls.
Retain product/host and explicitly approved timing exceptions. Manual Project sync-now and merge-observed issue effects are not interchangeable.
Use small ordinary Go/Python/TypeScript definitions and pure decisions where useful. A general statechart DSL, database, background daemon and single global machine are unnecessary.
Do not claim transactional rollback of a remote publication, message or merge. Reconcile actual outcome and use the owner’s documented recovery.
experience_acceptance: Truthful visible status and next action; no additional ordinary-work prompts; user changes survive uninstall; canceled UI/resources stay canceled.
Exercise success, refusal, interruption and resume from the user-facing owner. Record extra prompts and misleading readiness/empty-success states.
One owner for each capability, output class, state vocabulary and retry rule; generated derivatives stay consistent.
Change a contract once, regenerate the dependent catalog/schema/diagnostics, and prove all handlers/producers/consumers conform.
Discoverable current state, valid events, evidence scope, effect result and exact recovery action.
Require an agent to choose the next action from structured results without inferring permission, completion or retry safety from prose labels.
recommendation.limit: No finite audit can guarantee that every future change always improves all three experiences or never breaks anything. The enforceable objective is explicit compatibility invariants, measured acceptance criteria, discriminating event-sequence tests, exact-artifact checks and rollback for each migration slice.

migration: 0. Bind the baseline
Capture current command grammar, schemas, host events, file classes, exit codes and observable effects at the inspected commit. Label intended bug fixes separately.
All owners; source ledger and exact artifact inventories.
No behavior change. Replay the baseline before refactoring; preserve old records and package identities.
1. Repair closed contract mismatches
Fix preview-output recognition, operation discovery, launch-binding bound parity, tombstone history, Pi package identity and sidebar disposal.
Native producer/reader owners; shared hook owner; Pi owner.
Small independent regressions for each reproduced or statically proven sequence. Roll back one code/deployment slice without rewriting stored history or moving immutable release tags.
2. Make settlement and uncertainty explicit
Correct persona selection/delivery tracking; release receipt-only recovery; farm receipt recovery and containment propagation; distinguish failed sandbox inventory from empty inventory.
Hooks; release helper/workflow; farm runner; sandbox owner.
Inject failure after each external/local commit point. Prove read-back before retry and prohibit rerunning author work merely to recover a missing report.
3. Extract owned transition definitions
Add typed state/event/result definitions alongside current handlers; generate capability and output registries and diagnostic projections first.
Per-domain owners; no global cross-product state enum.
Differential replay preserves public effects, exit codes and rejected events except an explicit approved bugfix list. Preserve unknown fields/old reads as required by actual schemas.
4. Resolve actual policy decisions
Choose conflict stop scope, invalid-debug-packet correction, reviewer disposition, task progress/evidence invalidation, and any Pi child delegated authority design.
Maintainer decisions and owner implementation; amend affected ADRs.
These are intentional semantics changes and need a concrete reviewable proposal. Do not disguise them as an extraction/refactor.
5. Propagate and qualify

Update the owning host adapters; regenerate shared Python copies, surface/catalog projections and compiled bundles; validate exact built payloads. Propagate verified owner facts into site/reference content and separately scoped training compatibility.
core → generated adapters/build contracts → package checks → documentation/site → separately scoped Academy compatibility.
Platform/host matrix plus installed-artifact checks; then release per target. Keep tags immutable and original provenance/receipts.
approval_decisions: Whether a document-level conflict pauses only dependent work, with global host/user stops still global.
Whether corrected malformed packets can be resubmitted, and how severity differs from gate disposition.
Whether task-block/reconcile invalidation changes progress markers, evidence applicability, or both; define migration before changing old records.
Either implement an actually supported scoped parent delegation/audit path, or advertise the child capability as read-only until that exists.
Whether to add a registered bounded residue record for terminal harvest; keep ordinary work nonblocking.
Amend the specific ADR/compatibility/release-policy clauses that conflict with the selected implementation, using the normal acceptance owner.
verification_remaining: Native Go branches were fully read, but no Go toolchain was available in this workspace. Native composition failures are source-confirmed, not claimed as executed native integration tests.
The Python and Node probes use actual repository functions with temporary fixtures or injected host/Docker/terminal adapters. They do not constitute installed Claude, Codex or Pi host qualification.

No npm publication, GitHub Release mutation, remote Project/issue write, real Docker containment run or farm provider inference was performed. Publication and process recovery findings use source analysis and bounded pure probes.
Verify native writer/reader closure, launch-binding limits and tombstone preservation on the supported OS/architecture matrix and exact distributed binaries.
Exercise Pi activation/child tools/sidebar under the supported actual host runtime; verify cancellation and callback ordering with real UI and process lifetimes.
Exercise farm process-tree containment and report recovery with injected timeout, cleanup failure and final report-write failure; prove no surviving writer can race a reset/retry.
Exercise sandbox Docker output overflow, cancellation and failed removal; verify workload quiescence independently from client exit and preserve unknown inventory/cleanup outcomes.
Exercise release publication failure after the Release becomes public and before final codearbiter-publication.json attachment; rerun must complete missing evidence without retagging or republishing.
Qualify each exact released payload independently. Source on main, an accepted ADR, a successful packaging validator, or advisory exit0 is not a released-behavior guarantee.
claim_registry_delta: Current implementation facts
Product-specific; commit-bound

Development claim registry only; do not label main released.
Native observation contract
Product-specific with platform-specific behavior
Replace blanket read-lock/read-side-effect descriptions with operation- and platform-specific behavior.
Read mode, operation and platform belong in the claim key.
Context and evidence
Product-family shared, with explicit host/consumer exceptions
Distinguish ordinary assistive progress, optional strict consumers, provenance, delivery observations and host qualification.
Old audits and older mandatory-context claims need revalidation.
Pi capability
Surface-specific and release-specific
Separate current normal host support, the older narrow approval-entry code path and runtime gate, child execution capability and package identity.
Exact package/runtime evidence is required; no general approval support claim inferred.
Release and retirement
Product-specific policy; release-specific observations
Align publication recovery, pre-tag advisory/gating behavior and compatibility-removal metadata with one approved policy.
Publication/clock evidence remains release-specific.
Names and catalog counts
Shared product facts with surface-specific projections
Generate command grammar, lens counts, role summaries and hook delivery owner from canonical metadata.
Preserve legitimate host and product differences. No organization-global identity change is proposed.

machines.state_notation: Analytical phases over actual branches, subprocesses and evidence; literal verdicts and durable evidence states are identified in the rows.

transitions.effects: Reject invalid invocation through argparse before live activity.
transitions.failure_retry: A valid offline fixture is not a live host qualification.

transitions.guard: Exact declared cells, nonces, resource links, release provenance and hashes
transitions.effects: Hash fixture and evidence contract; collect explicit errors.
transitions.failure_retry: Required CLI/app-server cells are pinned to 0.143.0 and 0.145.0; advisory 0.149.0 is a separate class in this source snapshot.

transitions.guard: Neither durable report nor receipt directory exists
transitions.effects: Report absence without manufacturing successful backend evidence.
transitions.failure_retry: An offline PASS can coexist with pending durable evidence.

transitions.event: Validate report and all required receipts
transitions.guard: Exact membership, paths, duplicate-free JSON, hash binding, successful supported cells and observed policies
transitions.effects: Accept complete only if all required evidence is mutually consistent; otherwise preserve errors.
transitions.failure_retry: A partial report/receipt set cannot silently regress to pending or count advisory as required proof.

transitions.guard: Desktop-shell-proven must remain false in this contract
transitions.effects: Keep CLI/app-server result distinct from desktop shell behavior.
transitions.failure_retry: No hook-firing or desktop compatibility conclusion follows from these resource-read receipts alone.

machines.name: Isolated live resource probe and receipt classification
machines.state_storage: Ephemeral collector process, isolated temporary profile, exact candidate bytes, explicitly supplied durable receipts
machines.state_notation: Analytical phases over actual branches, subprocesses and evidence; literal verdicts and durable evidence states are identified in the rows.

transitions.event: Resolve exact binary and declared cell
transitions.guard: Pinned supported cell or explicitly advisory cell; binary is a regular file
transitions.effects: Resolve executable and fixture/contract hashes; create temporary isolated profile.
transitions.failure_retry: latest means this checker’s captured advisory release, not an unbounded current-version lookup.

transitions.guard: Actual hash equals declared native executable hash
transitions.effects: Hash mismatch returns failure before launching the candidate.
transitions.failure_retry: No inferred provenance from a requested version label.

transitions.guard: If supplied: exact controller-owned temp naming/containment and successful ChatGPT login status
transitions.effects: Build environment allowlist and separate profile/cache directories; inspect login without persisting raw output.
transitions.failure_retry: A supplied path outside the required cell root is rejected. A probe without supplied authentication does not become durable supported evidence merely by omitting the field.

transitions.guard: Exact binary invoked; actual returned version and installation results checked
transitions.effects: Install local fixture marketplace and plugin through host commands; compare installed bytes under isolated plugin root.
transitions.failure_retry: Version/install errors accumulate; some later steps still run to produce evidence rather than turning a failed preflight into success.

transitions.guard: read-only sandbox, never approval, disabled web search, exact entry and two linked resources
transitions.effects: Run ephemeral structured-output turn; collect completed command events, paths and nonces.
transitions.failure_retry: Each subprocess has a timeout; CLI TimeoutExpired/OSError is not universally converted into a receipt by this path.

transitions.guard: Exactly one valid host invocation or one verified direct entry read; exactly three allowed successful direct reads
transitions.effects: Bind actual executable, installed bytes, fixture, policy and sanitized canonical evidence hashes.
transitions.failure_retry: Agent-reported paths/nonces alone are insufficient; fallback searches or mismatched command events fail.

transitions.guard: Secret checks or unsafe error text
transitions.effects: Replace persisted error text with constant classification and clear unsafe evidence hashes.
transitions.failure_retry: Raw streams are not copied into the receipt; failure-classification hashes are not successful transcript evidence.

transitions.effects: Supported PASS exits0, supported FAIL exits1; advisory returns0 even with FAIL.
transitions.failure_retry: Exit0 alone therefore does not prove qualification; consumers must read verdict and evidence_class.

transitions.effects: Remove generated temporary marketplace/profile.
transitions.failure_retry: A separately supplied controller-owned authenticated home is not owned by TemporaryDirectory cleanup.

machines.name: App-server JSONL protocol and shutdown
machines.state_storage: Ephemeral collector process, isolated temporary profile, exact candidate bytes, explicitly supplied durable receipts
machines.state_notation: Analytical phases over actual branches, subprocesses and evidence; literal verdicts and durable evidence states are identified in the rows.

transitions.guard: Exact executable and isolated environment selected
transitions.effects: Launch process; start stdout queue and stderr reader threads.
transitions.failure_retry: Streams/message lists are retained in memory; per-read timeout is not a total session deadline or global output cap.

transitions.guard: Matching request id, object result and correct codexHome
transitions.effects: Send initialized notification, then skills/list with forceReload.
transitions.failure_retry: Error response, malformed JSON, EOF or missing response raises a protocol failure.

transitions.guard: Exactly one namespaced selected skill, absolute installed path and matching bytes
transitions.effects: Bind selected skill and installed root.
transitions.failure_retry: Missing, duplicate or relative skill selection cannot advance as successful proof.

transitions.guard: Thread id and actual effective readOnly sandbox with networkAccess=false
transitions.effects: Request never approval and ephemeral thread; retain observed effective policies.
transitions.failure_retry: Requested policy does not replace the returned effective policy.

transitions.guard: Explicit skill input plus constrained read instructions
transitions.effects: Collect notification stream until turn/completed; record completed command events.
transitions.failure_retry: Every _next wait is bounded20seconds; continuous notifications can extend the overall operation.

transitions.guard: Completed status and valid final agent JSON plus successful exact command evidence
transitions.effects: Inject host-observed requested/effective policy into observation and validate through common receipt builder.
transitions.failure_retry: Non-completed status or protocol failure yields errors; the last textual claim is not sufficient.

transitions.effects: Close stdin, wait2seconds, terminate then kill on successive timeouts, join reader threads and close streams.
transitions.failure_retry: This is bounded staged shutdown of the direct process; it is not a claim of arbitrary descendant-process containment.

machines.name: Candidate package snapshot and resource closure
machines.state_storage: Ephemeral collector process, isolated temporary profile, exact candidate bytes, explicitly supplied durable receipts
machines.state_notation: Analytical phases over actual branches, subprocesses and evidence; literal verdicts and durable evidence states are identified in the rows.

transitions.guard: Regular non-symlink/reparse root and supported shape
transitions.effects: Reject unsafe entries, encrypted ZIP members, invalid modes, path escapes, normalized collisions and expansion limits.
transitions.failure_retry: Validation does not install or execute candidate bytes.

transitions.guard: Same device/inode as enumerated regular file; size within declared bounds
transitions.effects: Read bounded bytes and reject changes beyond declared size; verify permitted promoted large binaries against receipt hashes.
transitions.failure_retry: Large-file exception is narrow and receipt-bound, not a general bypass of candidate bounds.

transitions.guard: Any selected helper/consumer marker activates the whole required local set
transitions.effects: Require named helper/consumer resources and expected contract entry markers.
transitions.failure_retry: Marker presence is static packaging evidence, not proof that runtime delivery succeeds.

transitions.guard: UTF8 and supported link grammar; contained resolvable local Markdown links or named templates
transitions.effects: Record selected file hashes and relative-read edges in deterministic order.
transitions.failure_retry: Remote links are not fetched; approved symbolic template destinations are not mistaken for concrete existing files.

transitions.guard: ca-codex identity, valid version, names match paths, exact approved hook manifest digest and present targets
transitions.effects: Produce package/resource digests and selected paths.
transitions.failure_retry: An approved hook inventory digest proves the static contract only, not host hook invocation.

transitions.effects: Print structured or human result.
transitions.failure_retry: No live authenticated turn or publication is implied by this lane.

machines.name: Constrained Markdown link parser context
machines.state_storage: Ephemeral collector process, isolated temporary profile, exact candidate bytes, explicitly supplied durable receipts
machines.state_notation: Analytical phases over actual branches, subprocesses and evidence; literal verdicts and durable evidence states are identified in the rows.

transitions.event: Open fenced/quoted/list/indented code or HTML literal
transitions.guard: Recognized grammar and current fence/indent state
transitions.effects: Blank literal characters while preserving offsets/newlines; retain specially recognized symbolic destination segments.
transitions.failure_retry: A filename match inside code or an HTML literal is not automatically a resource edge.

transitions.guard: Matching fence character/length, quote/list continuation rules
transitions.effects: Resume link interpretation outside literal regions.
transitions.failure_retry: Unmatched literal delimiters retain their actual parser behavior; not a general CommonMark library guarantee.

transitions.guard: Matched delimiter or recognized literal form
transitions.effects: Ignore code spans, escaped references and image-like regions for resource links.
transitions.failure_retry: An unmatched code span is left visible by this scanner.

transitions.guard: Balanced labels, parentheses depth<=32 and supported optional title
transitions.effects: Unescape supported punctuation and return target with occupied span.
transitions.failure_retry: Malformed/unsupported/unterminated destination or title raises explicit ValueError.

transitions.guard: Unique normalized label; existing definition for full/collapsed reference
transitions.effects: Resolve supported full/collapsed/defined shortcut references outside occupied spans.
transitions.failure_retry: Duplicate or unresolved reference-style definitions fail instead of guessing a target.

transitions.guard: Opening/closing delimiter, unique allowed key grammar and required nonempty fields
transitions.effects: Decode supported quoted scalar values and verify name/path relation in package owner.
transitions.failure_retry: Multiline/unsupported front matter is rejected by this deliberately constrained parser, not silently interpreted as YAML.

machines.name: Operation admission, lock ownership and store availability
machines.explicitness: implicit control state over files and guards
machines.state_storage: native file handles; Windows store.lock; Linux root descriptor; Darwin lock file

transitions.effects: Return process capabilities/schema without opening repository.
transitions.failure_retry: Invalid request or unknown operation rejects before repository effects.

transitions.effects: Open root-anchored filesystem and operation-local memo.
transitions.failure_retry: Unsupported platform/unsafe root refuse.

transitions.guard: operation in sharedObservation, or read mode exact
transitions.effects: Acquire shared lock for selected read operations. Windows observation requires existing store metadata; Linux needs none. Darwin lock path may create store.lock.
transitions.failure_retry: Busy: bounded 2s retry then LOCK_TIMEOUT; fresh read advised. Missing Windows metadata: NO_LOCAL_STORE.

transitions.effects: Acquire exclusive lock; index remains exclusive despite being observational. Windows index uses read-access ObservationLock.
transitions.failure_retry: LOCK_FAILED / LOCK_TIMEOUT; no semantic mutation.

transitions.effects: Initialize platform lock metadata only; report created or present. Linux reports present.
transitions.failure_retry: Native filesystem failures remain explicit.

transitions.guard: operation is not recovery or successful replay
transitions.effects: Refuse normal canonical reads and writes until deliberate recovery.
transitions.failure_retry: RECOVERY_REQUIRED; use existing transaction ID, not blind new mutation ID.

transitions.effects: Unlock and close filesystem; discard per-operation memo.
transitions.failure_retry: No daemon or persistent in-memory coordinator.

machines.name: Journaled transaction and operation identity
machines.explicitness: explicit persisted journal states plus implicit staging and acknowledgement states
machines.state_storage: transactions/<operation_id>.json; stage files; history before-images; stored result

transitions.guard: valid id/hash, <=512 safe disjoint edits, exact before bytes, no pending journal
transitions.effects: Write synced before-images and destination stages; create directories as needed; retain request hash and result.
transitions.failure_retry: Prepublication errors clean temporary stages/backups when safe; no target changes.

transitions.effects: Durably publish full write intent before touching canonical targets.
transitions.failure_retry: Publication uncertainty returns COMMIT_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN and preserves recovery material.

transitions.guard: current target still equals its before hash
transitions.effects: Replace/create/delete targets sequentially; may expose partial files only behind recovery block.
transitions.failure_retry: Any failure after publication returns COMMIT_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN; do not assume no change.

transitions.effects: Persist committed journal including original result and before-image references.
transitions.failure_retry: Final acknowledgement write failure is outcome unknown; inspect/replay same operation ID.

transitions.effects: Return stored original outcome with replay=true; no new revision, no repeated effect.
transitions.failure_retry: Old journals without result require refresh_required, not fabricated latest identity.

transitions.effects: Refuse operation-id reuse.
transitions.failure_retry: OPERATION_ID_REUSE; new logical intent needs new ID.

transitions.effects: Refuse ordinary replay pending recovery.
transitions.failure_retry: RECOVERY_REQUIRED.

transitions.effects: Refuse resurrecting rolled-back write.
transitions.failure_retry: OPERATION_ROLLED_BACK; inspect then explicitly choose new operation.

machines.name: Recovery and recovery conflicts
machines.explicitness: explicit terminal states; inferred conflict and partial target position
machines.state_storage: journal plus current target/stage/backup digests

transitions.guard: all targets currently before or after; every necessary stage verified before any write
transitions.effects: Complete missing edits, clean verified unused stages, persist terminal state.
transitions.failure_retry: RECOVERY_CONFLICT for third-party edits; COMMIT_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN for I/O interruption; retry same recovery.

transitions.guard: all current targets before or after; backups hash-valid before any write
transitions.effects: Restore old bytes/delete new targets, clean stages, preserve transaction/history.
transitions.failure_retry: All-target preflight prevents overwriting outside changes; incomplete recovery stays prepared.

transitions.effects: Return replay without reapplying inverse/forward edits.
transitions.failure_retry: Recovery is not general undo of a committed arbitrary write.

transitions.event: target has third digest / missing recovery material
transitions.effects: No preflight mutation; preserve evidence for manual reconciliation.
transitions.failure_retry: RECOVERY_CONFLICT; must resolve actual bytes before retry.

transitions.guard: invalid shape/name/path/hash, unreadable, listed file disappears
transitions.effects: Refuse to treat store as clean.
transitions.failure_retry: CORRUPT_JOURNAL / RECOVERY_REQUIRED / I/O diagnostic.

machines.name: Artifact representation, version and canonical identity
machines.explicitness: implicit control state over files and guards
machines.state_storage: HTML embedded model, schema_version, normative/model hashes and catalog

transitions.guard: closed supported kind and schema, unique identity/path
transitions.effects: Create revision 1, typed normative state, presentation, checksums; plan tasks PENDING, governance draft.
transitions.failure_retry: Duplicate identity, existing canonical slug or catalog bounds refuse.

transitions.guard: historical schema supported and no newer fields mislabeled
transitions.effects: Validate and expose without automatic upgrade or recertification.
transitions.failure_retry: Unsupported versions/assistive fields under old labels fail closed.

transitions.effects: Write appropriate 0.3.2/0.3.3 schema while retaining history.
transitions.failure_retry: No silent reinterpretation on read.

transitions.guard: unique ID; correct directory/kind; no same-slug HTML+Markdown
transitions.to: valid catalog or invalid or ambiguous
transitions.effects: Spec and plan directories remain strict on catalog scans; optional kinds read only when active.
transitions.failure_retry: One invalid strict spec/plan can reject unrelated catalog-based operation; selected work avoids broad catalog.

machines.name: Artifact governance and semantic revision
machines.explicitness: explicit draft/approved with derived authority validity; ready/superseded admitted by schema without public transition writers
machines.state_storage: governance.state, approval history, current normative identity

transitions.guard: Ready + current exact approval receipt; plan bound approved_source to approved spec; allowed authority profile
transitions.effects: Append approval, increment revision, render and journal artifact.
transitions.failure_retry: Generic approve refuses sprint_pair/SMARTS profiles; invalid/stale receipt never changes state.

transitions.guard: valid closed changes alter normative hash
transitions.effects: Keep historical approvals; revision advances; surviving execution progress preserved.
transitions.failure_retry: CAS and structural errors refuse whole batch.

transitions.effects: Increment model revision/hash only; normative identity unchanged.
transitions.failure_retry: No approval or receipt fabricated.

transitions.event: approval chain unavailable or subject changes
transitions.effects: Expose derived authority status without rewriting stored progress.
transitions.failure_retry: Strict authority consumers reject; ordinary progress can remain available.

machines.name: Stable symbol lifecycle
machines.explicitness: explicit retirement records; allocation history implicit in stable IDs
machines.state_storage: symbol index; normative records; retired_symbols

transitions.guard: valid collection; ID never active/retired/allocated in same batch
transitions.effects: Add stable record; sync execution for new tasks/prerequisites; increment revision.
transitions.failure_retry: ID reuse rejected; whole batch atomic.

transitions.guard: same immutable ID/kind; exact permitted fields or permutation
transitions.effects: Change fields/order; semantic validation then one journaled artifact save.
transitions.failure_retry: Kind/ID edits, dangling references or invalid reorder refuse.

transitions.guard: reason supplied; references remain valid; no conflicting orphan execution state
transitions.effects: Remove live record; append immutable tombstone with retiring revision/replacement.
transitions.failure_retry: Missing reason, tombstone editing, invalid replacement or dangling links refuse. Retiring tasks with check history currently fails due to N-F10.

transitions.effects: Reject resurrection or rewriting historical identity.
transitions.failure_retry: New logical record must use new ID.

machines.name: Readiness, open decisions and criterion coverage
machines.explicitness: explicit nested statuses; readiness derived, not stored authorization
machines.state_storage: normative open_decisions, criteria, dispositions; derived validation

transitions.effects: Update normative record; formerly blocking readiness may clear.
transitions.failure_retry: Resolved without resolution is structurally invalid.

transitions.effects: Retain explicit unresolved state; blocking decision causes Ready failure.
transitions.failure_retry: No specialized irreversible transition policy: generic apply permits reopening. Deferred is a criterion disposition or decomposition question state, not a spec open-decision status.

transitions.guard: all required semantic fields; named tests for test commands; DAG/partition/input coverage; spec criterion mapping
transitions.effects: Return deterministic diagnostics; does not approve.
transitions.failure_retry: OPEN_BLOCKER, uncovered criterion/scope/input, invalid command etc remain diagnostic.

transitions.effects: Refuse active not-applicable criterion or mandatory criterion disposition.
transitions.failure_retry: Must explicitly revise/retire outcome with reason; no automatic task execution.

machines.name: Plan–spec binding currency
machines.explicitness: implicit control state over files and guards
machines.state_storage: plan.normative.spec_ref and source normative hash

transitions.guard: same-slug Ready pair; exact spec_expected CAS when explicit draft mode
transitions.effects: Bind current spec digest; preserve execution/history; plan governance remains/resets draft, revision advances.
transitions.failure_retry: Concurrent source change or invalid pair refuses; no source approval invented.

transitions.guard: valid current spec; actual authority assessed
transitions.effects: Choose approved_source only when genuine source approval valid; preserve work state.
transitions.failure_retry: No approval receipt required just to rebind ordinary plan.

transitions.effects: Advisory consumers report binding_current=false; strict Ready/authority consumers reject.
transitions.failure_retry: Task-start and ordinary reporting do not silently rebind or auto-clear stop.

machines.state_storage: plan.execution.tasks[id].state, reason, historical evidence refs

transitions.guard: task live; CAS; no receipt/context-ticket/approval required
transitions.effects: Record implementation start; no source snapshot or verification evidence.
transitions.failure_retry: Any nonPENDING source returns NOT_PENDING, preserving blocked/active state.

transitions.effects: Record implementation ready for review, evidence refs unchanged.
transitions.failure_retry: Other source states refuse; partial evidence fields never downgrade to ordinary path.

transitions.effects: Record correction/resume with reason, retain evidence; ordinary reconcile does not call invalidateDependents.
transitions.failure_retry: No proof or approval claim; protocol rejects other targets.

transitions.effects: Record stop; mark transitive dependents STALE except already PENDING/BLOCKED; preserve receipts.
transitions.failure_retry: Does not automatically restart or clear another blocked task.

transitions.effects: Record implementation done without claiming tests or review passed; schema 0.3.2.
transitions.failure_retry: PENDING/BLOCKED/STALE member refuses complete scope.

machines.name: Strict receipted task review, reconciliation and acceptance

machines.state_storage: task state/evidence refs; scope baselines; current full input identity

transitions.guard: Ready approved plan+spec, approved_source binding, strict prereqs, current snapshot, both exact receipts, completion rules
transitions.effects: Append both refs, set/retain exact completion receipt selection; establish scope baseline if absent.
transitions.failure_retry: Stale plan baseline needs scope-reconcile; failed/missing named tests/stale refs reject.

transitions.guard: current reconciliation receipt exact input/task/target; REVIEW additionally TaskFresh
transitions.effects: Append evidence/reason; target other than REVIEW transitively invalidates dependents.
transitions.failure_retry: Invalid receipt/input/claim rejects all changes.

transitions.guard: current exact reconciliation receipt for scope/input
transitions.effects: Set base input and plan hashes; append reconciliation to member tasks.
transitions.failure_retry: Preserve prior evidence; cannot silently convert stale baseline.

transitions.guard: previous checkpoint accepted fresh; every member TaskFresh; exact current quality/completion evidence
transitions.effects: Accept entire scope atomically, append quality receipt.
transitions.failure_retry: Any failed member or prior scope refuses entire transition.

transitions.effects: Project all_accepted_and_current only when every task ACCEPTED, fresh, no conflicting checks or unassessed trimmed history.
transitions.failure_retry: May fail due to approval, stale source, infrastructure or missing evidence; never treats DONE/REVIEW as verification.

machines.name: Dependency invalidation and advisory scheduling

machines.state_storage: task DAG, execution states, scoped prerequisites; derived advice

transitions.guard: all transitive dependencies REVIEW/DONE/ACCEPTED; scoped prereqs satisfied
transitions.effects: List candidate and first next_task; binding currency and prerequisites reported separately.
transitions.failure_retry: Unknown/missing dependencies explicit; no authority granted.

transitions.effects: Report exact blockers; unscoped legacy prereqs reported without inventing global scope.
transitions.failure_retry: Unrelated tasks can remain eligible.

transitions.event: task-block or strict reconcile nonREVIEW on ancestor
transitions.effects: Change progress label and reason, retain historical refs.
transitions.failure_retry: Plain ordinary reconcile differs: does not propagate this invalidation.

transitions.effects: No persisted scheduling ticket or worker dispatch; task-start checks duplicate start separately.
transitions.failure_retry: Advice can become stale before action; CAS protects mutation, not user intent.

transitions.effects: Record caller_reported origin,time,definition digest; legacy flag/evidence not overwritten.

transitions.effects: Expose stale observation as unknown, retain original.
transitions.failure_retry: No automatic recertification.

transitions.guard: historical receipt not live assessed here
transitions.effects: Report recorded legacy flag separately.
transitions.failure_retry: Never silently promote old satisfied flag into fresh observed fact.

transitions.guard: strict guards+snapshot; exact current prerequisite receipt
transitions.effects: Delete ordinary observation for ID, set legacy satisfied and append receipt.
transitions.failure_retry: Strict consumers require legacy receipts and reject presence of ordinary observation.

transitions.effects: Append inert caller_reported result, operation identity/time, task+criterion subject, bounded scoped source fingerprint if obtainable.

transitions.effects: Drop oldest current record; prior history remains journal before-image.

transitions.guard: current task verification/path/criteria/constraint identity and partial input digest

transitions.to: current only if old exact subject still matches

transitions.failure_retry: No retroactive narrower authority.

transitions.effects: Exclude from current conflict and disclose ignored count.
transitions.failure_retry: Unassessed failure retained; no assumption it is obsolete.

transitions.effects: Surface unassessed history to explicit verification consumers.
transitions.failure_retry: Strict all-accepted cannot claim current verification from unknown lost history.

transitions.guard: receipt validated and captures exact report hashes

transitions.failure_retry: Later otherwise identical report has distinct recording_operation_id and remains visible.

transitions.guard: exact selected subject + inputs; activity-specific guards
transitions.effects: Create immutable context describing exact subject/prompt/review material; no progress change.
transitions.failure_retry: Stale or mismatched subject rejects.

transitions.effects: Read historical v0.1 evidence without relabeling current.
transitions.failure_retry: Missing/tampered chain rejects inspection.

transitions.effects: Validate actual evidence links, not actor text/comments.
transitions.failure_retry: Historical authority rejected; actual host/user permission remains separate.

findings.title: Conflict command prescribes a broader stop than the assistive engine contract
findings.detail: The conflict command says all work stops when governing rules conflict. Current sprint/context guidance and ADR0043 describe refusal scoped to dependent work. These cannot both be a universal rule. Source does not implement a single dependency-aware conflict controller.
findings.recommendation: Choose and document the stop scope explicitly. Recommend stop affected authority/data dependencies, preserve independent read-only work, and keep genuine global host/user stops global. This is a policy decision, not a silent prose cleanup.

findings.title: Debug handoff treats a correctable packet error as a terminal one-shot boundary
findings.detail: The workflow forbids repairing and resubmitting any rejected packet. The validator is stateless and distinguishes malformed/invalid packets from internal I/O errors; it records no consumed one-shot capability. The prose therefore imposes an extra recovery policy beyond implementation.
findings.recommendation: Separate invalid input, denied authority, stale binding and internal failure. Permit an explicitly corrected new input attempt where authority remains valid; retain the refusal for an unchanged denied request. Requires approved workflow-policy change.

findings.title: Maintenance severity and reviewer disposition conflict
findings.detail: The dependency reviewer can report HIGH maintenance risk while saying not to block on maintenance alone. The included reviewer contract says every HIGH is blocking and additions never replace that rule. This makes a correct verdict ambiguous for the reviewing agent and user.
findings.recommendation: Represent severity and disposition separately; document the explicit maintenance-only disposition exception or revise its severity. Generate the common verdict contract from the selected policy.

findings.title: Terminal finding harvest has no implemented recovery for interruption before the terminal step
findings.detail: Several workflows harvest qualifying findings at completion. The knowledge helper and session/standup paths do not implement a durable pending-harvest backstop. An interrupted run can therefore leave eligible findings only in conversation; the source does not prove every such finding is lost.
findings.recommendation: Keep harvest opportunistic. If durable recovery is desired, record bounded pending candidates at discovery and settle/deduplicate on completion/resume. Register any new output with all native readers; do not introduce a new universal completion gate.

findings.title: SessionStart persona documentation contradicts the prompt-submit owner
findings.detail: Init/porting language attributes persona injection to SessionStart. The implemented SessionStart path and ADR0030 place full composed persona delivery in UserPromptSubmit; a mode revisitation bug is documented separately in the hooks findings.
findings.recommendation: Make prompt-submit the documented delivery owner and distinguish session setup, selected mode, committed mode and delivered persona.

findings.title: Sensitive-lines-only override wording understates the implemented candidate binding
findings.detail: The override surface describes an invalidation scope around sensitive lines. The security pass and binding helper retain full candidate/worktree/sensitive digests and hash the complete staged UTF8 diff. A user cannot reliably predict grant reuse from the narrower wording.
findings.recommendation: Document the exact binding tuple and invalidation event. Preserve current security semantics while deriving override help from the same binding definition.

findings.title: Watch confuses absence of agent polling with absence of CLI polling
findings.detail: The watch command describes gh pr checks --watch as server-side blocking with no polling interval. The official gh command documents --interval with default10seconds. Waiting in one detached CLI invocation avoids model-driven polling, but the underlying CLI still refreshes periodically.
findings.recommendation: Say one detached gh watch process with no repeated agent calls; preserve its timeout/cancel behavior. Correct the no-polling claim.

findings.title: Command catalog and reviewer index drift from their owner bodies
findings.detail: COMMANDS.md calls Tribunal eleven-lens while the current owner/reference set contains thirteen. Its release signature uses --dry-run and SemVer-only language where the current owner uses --dryrun and supports numeric sequence targets. The agent index also presents coverage behavior more strongly than the coverage reviewer body does.
findings.recommendation: Generate signatures, lens count and index descriptions from explicit owner metadata; do not change actual command spelling or verdict rules just to match stale summaries.

findings.title: Compatibility-removal metadata encodes a different policy than the public owner
findings.detail: command-routes.json removalRequires is minor-release-with-changelog-notice. build-surface.py enforces that literal vocabulary. The command compatibility policy describes a major/1.0 floor plus a separate approved removal decision and fresh evidence. The release-state observer does not enforce removalRequires. This is a dormant metadata/policy conflict, not proof of an unauthorized live alias removal.
findings.recommendation: Choose the approved retirement rule, give it one owner and generate both policy prose and accepted registry values. Preserve existing aliases until the separately approved removal conditions are met.

findings.title: Ordinary context previews poison strict snapshot output recognition
findings.detail: contextOrdinaryPreview calls PutDerived("context-previews"), but internalOutputsWith does not allow that reserved directory. Any successful preview therefore creates a directory that a subsequent strict Snapshot refuses as UNRECOGNIZED_OUTPUT. Completion normalized workspace scanning shares the same recognizer. Ordinary progress can still work; strict verification, review/quality/farm consumers can fail.
findings.recommendation: Add a closed validated context-preview output contract and exercise preview→snapshot→completion composition. Do not broadly ignore arbitrary .artifacts contents.

findings.title: Implemented repair-apply absent from capability operation list
findings.detail: protocol RequestSchema and JournaledMutation and Run support repair-apply; operations list returned by Names excludes it. Agent capability discovery cannot enumerate this implemented event.
findings.recommendation: Derive operation names, request dispatch coverage, side-effect class and lock policy from one repository-owned typed registry, with exhaustive coverage checks.

findings.status: source-confirmed semantics; intent requires product decision
findings.title: Ordinary reconciliation and blocking propagate different task-state invalidation
findings.detail: task-block calls invalidateDependents and writes STALE to every transitive dependent except PENDING/BLOCKED. Receipt-free task-reconcile changes selected state without invalidating dependents; receipted nonREVIEW reconciliation does invalidate. Stored STALE conflates progress and evidence/dependency assessment, despite ADR-0043 stating those are separate.
findings.recommendation: Specify existing branches explicitly; keep stored compatibility states for now, add orthogonal dependency/evidence assessments. Change propagation only through a versioned deliberate semantic migration with blocked-stop tests.

findings.title: Two kinds of review completion share REVIEW and accept-scope dispatch
findings.detail: Ordinary task-review means implementation reported ready, strict task-review means exact verification+review chain consumed; both store REVIEW. Ordinary accept-scope records DONE while strict path records ACCEPTED. The difference depends on request fields and available evidence, so event names alone are insufficient.
findings.recommendation: Expose effect/claim semantics and allowed next events in operation metadata/structured context; preserve legacy wire names and receipts.

findings.title: Read-side effects depend on operation mode and platform
findings.detail: Contextual read writes content-addressed delivery tokens; exact read does not. Darwin shared nativeLock invokes lockFile which creates metadata if absent. Windows shared observations explicitly require existing metadata and never initialize; Linux locks repository directory. The initStore comment "Reads never initialize" is too broad for Darwin.
findings.recommendation: Represent read-only/metadata-writing/external-effect traits explicitly and state native platform differences precisely; do not infer mutation class from command name.

findings.title: Stored check-status vocabulary exceeds reachable public mutation behavior
findings.detail: Work schema and renderers permit/display unknown/passed/failed, but work create/adoption initialize unknown and all native implemented lifecycle updates leave check_status unchanged. This is schema capacity, not proof of an implemented passed/failed event.
findings.recommendation: Classify schema-only states as such in machine contract/capabilities; do not invent an event or migrate progress into proof.

findings.title: Task context does inspect scoped source for recorded checks
findings.detail: taskContext comment says it does not inspect source files. It calls assessTaskChecks, which invokes scopedInputDigest and reads bounded declared paths, shared inputs and known build manifests.
findings.recommendation: Correct the bounded-read claim; keep source-scope disclosure in context output and performance expectations.

findings.title: Unsupported-platform message still describes Windows/macOS as pending
findings.detail: fs_other.unsupported says repository operations require Linux and Windows/macOS promotion pending; supported Darwin/Windows build files enable NativeWrites with actual backends. This is stale diagnostic prose, not evidence those supported platforms are disabled.
findings.recommendation: Generate platform capability text from current backend declaration or restrict diagnostic to unsupported GOOS without making release claims.

findings.status: Producer output reproduced in Python; native rejection source-confirmed only
findings.title: Valid npm launch bindings exceed native completion consumer cap
findings.detail: commandBindingSchema accepts 37 launch files and validateQualifiedBinding accepts 32 workspace manifests. completionWorkspacesOnce rejects any launch_files length above32. Hooks agent exercised actual Python _bind_commands with real temporary Git/npm fixtures:31 workspace manifests produced33 launch files;32 produced34 on POSIX. Windows adapted npm source can produce37. Evidence stored in audit-work/probe_launch_binding_results.json; no native Go test executed.
findings.recommendation: Use one role-aware binding bound across producer, schema and consumer; add boundary fixtures at32/33/37 with actual npm layouts without executing stored commands.

findings.title: Retirement with retained task checks or scope baselines is rejected as orphan state
findings.detail: syncExecution removes retired live task states but retains task_check_observations and existing scopes. Changes appends tombstones under retired_symbols. symbol.Build gives these tombstones Kind=retired_symbols; planStructure accepts historical checks for nonlive IDs only when Retired and Kind=tasks, impossible for the emitted tombstone. render.Prepare calls Structural, so task retirement after task-check fails ORPHAN_STATE. Removing a checkpoint with retained scope baseline similarly yields ORPHAN_STATE because syncExecution does not retire/remove scope entries.
findings.recommendation: Define retired-state ownership explicitly: preserve original record kind or validate history against an explicit typed retirement record; archive/retire scope baselines consistently. Preserve original evidence and journal history; do not simply delete checks to make retirement pass.

findings.title: Returning to an already delivered mode suppresses the current persona
findings.evidence_level: focused isolated runtime probe + implementation read
findings.description: Delivery is keyed by session, mode and compaction generation. In one session/generation, arbiter -> dangerous -> arbiter leaves the original arbiter tuple marked, so the final arbiter effective mode emits no arbiter persona after dangerous was injected.
findings.observed: Actual shared mode writes/audits and actual persona files: initial arbiter output10990 characters; dangerous7908; return to arbiter0. This does not disable deterministic tool/Git guards.
findings.recommendation: Bind delivery to current successful mode transition epoch or last delivered mode/generation, with monotonic session identity; preserve repeated-event idempotency and independent safety injection.
findings.status: focused isolated runtime probe + implementation read

findings.title: Mode flip failure reports no change after raw state has already changed
findings.evidence_level: isolated injected append failure + implementation read
findings.description: flip writes raw mode before audit settlement. An audit append failure returns FLIP_FAILED; prompt text calls it a marker write error and says the session remains in its current mode. The raw mode can already be ops while effective mode falls back to arbiter because it is not ledger-backed.
findings.observed: With _append_override_line forced false: result failed, raw_mode ops, effective_mode arbiter, user_message says marker write error and remains in current mode. Owed audit recovery is implemented; failure is not evidence of total rollback.
findings.recommendation: Return typed outcome carrying requested/raw/effective modes, marker commit and audit debt/retry state. Report partial completion honestly; preserve existing recovery and gate fail direction.
findings.status: isolated injected append failure + implementation read

findings.title: Qualified npm workspace binding can exceed native completion consumer limit
findings.classification: confirmed producer reachability; cross-layer consumer mismatch validated by native agent

findings.description: The Python producer permits up to32 workspace manifests plus base launch files. findings.title: Spinner uninstall restores backup over a user change made after install
findings.evidence_level: isolated settings transformation probe + implementation read
findings.description: statusLine uninstall checks exact ownership before restoring. _uninstall_spinner_verbs restores whenever its backup key exists, even if current spinnerVerbs was changed by the user after installation.
findings.observed: Current verbs user changed after install plus prior backup becomes prior, losing the current choice.
findings.recommendation: Record exact installed spinner ownership value and restore backup only if current still equals it; otherwise preserve current custom state and remove obsolete backup metadata.

findings.title: Debug validator rejection is stateless and does not prove authorization denial
findings.description: _debughandofflib imports no filesystem/process/network facility and maintains no rejection ledger. Each CLI invocation independently validates shape/references/internal semantics. Exit2 includes correctable input failures; exit3 operational failures. Root audit should compare one-shot resubmission prose against this distinction.
findings.recommendation: Separate invalid transport/shape/reference input, unsupported causal evidence and denied authorization in the contract. Allow bounded correction of shape for the same authorized scope without silently widening authority; preserve substantive causal/regression requirements.

findings.title: Per-turn prompt owns persona delivery; SessionStart owns startup side effects
findings.description: prompt-submit composes/dedups safety and mode persona, and PreCompact changes delivery generation. SessionStart does mode housekeeping/statusline repair before activation, installs Git backstop when active, then initialized briefing and detached refresh. Documentation claiming persona injection is owned solely by SessionStart is stale.
findings.recommendation: Generate event-to-owner documentation from the implemented hook contract and retain a passive explicit-root inspection route for unfamiliar repos.

findings.title: Security review marker binds the complete staged candidate, not just sensitive lines
findings.description: The marker includes worktree identity, whole staged diff binding and sensitive diagnostics. Consumer requires all matching. Unrelated staged edits invalidate this proof. Producing the marker does not independently verify semantic reviewer PASS; the higher-level workflow owns that obligation.
findings.recommendation: Document the actual candidate boundary and generate recovery text from it; preserve complete-diff invalidation until an intentionally reviewed narrower evidence model exists.

findings.title: No startup or knowledge backstop scans stranded terminal harvest residue
findings.classification: confirmed absence within inspected entrypoint/helper scope
findings.evidence_level: complete executable-source read of relevant runtime family
findings.description: SessionStart daily standup checks Git/task/provenance/update state, and knowledge.py handles selected native knowledge edits/conversion/promotion/staleness. Neither implements a durable scan for an unharvested terminal workflow obligation. Root prose audit owns whether such an obligation is promised.
findings.recommendation: If harvest is mandatory, persist an explicit retryable per-workflow obligation and expose it in status/recovery; do not infer obligations from unrelated board prose or rerun successful external effects.

findings.title: Native client accepts optional context qualification field
findings.description: ArtifactClient._open_binary accepts either five release-manifest fields or those plus context_qualification. The farm consumer exact-five check found by host agent has a narrower acceptance set. Python method does not itself validate optional field value.
findings.recommendation: Use one versioned manifest schema for producers and consumers, retaining explicit platform/native-tested/digest checks. Host/native ledgers own candidate qualification effects.

findings.title: Pi author child has no usable mutation authorization path
findings.implication: The role advertises write/edit/bash but the default execute policy asks for every mutator and the child has RPC UI. The child also lacks the approved-permission audit callback. Successful handshake/read capability therefore does not imply author capability.
findings.recommendation: Keep final guard fail-closed; define a parent-issued task-scoped delegated capability with explicit paths/commands, expiry/session/generation, and parent-owned durable audit. Until that contract exists, advertise this child role as read-only/unavailable for authorship.

findings.implication: A persona read failure is stored as bridge degradation after readiness. A later successful bridge refresh can clear that degraded state while persona remains empty, with no persona retry edge.
findings.recommendation: Make persona loading an explicit prerequisite or a durable independent unavailable capability. Ready/governed rendering must depend on the same actual prerequisite vector as prompt construction.

findings.title: Qualified production artifact manifests are rejected by farm parser
findings.implication: Farm accepts exact top-level keys format/version/protocol/schema_version/binaries. Promotion adds context_qualification, and production cold execution requires the current platform in that field. Thus a production-qualified manifest shape fails farm admission before native binary execution. This is current-source incompatibility, not an assertion that a particular published release was observed failing.
findings.recommendation: Use one versioned release-manifest decoder/contract across farm, installers and verification; explicitly admit and validate the supported optional context field. Add an exact qualified-package farm admission test before loosening any trust checks.

findings.title: Farm receipt failure is not a safe author-redispatch instruction
findings.implication: Exit 3 can follow successful task commits/merges and integration worktree cleanup. A new invocation force-resets integration to base and replaces same task branches/worktrees. Reused FARM_RUN_ID also opens an existing run directory and truncates stream evidence.
findings.recommendation: Split recover-receipt from retry-author. Persist an exclusive run identity and durable task/integration commit references, inspect existing refs on recovery, and reproduce missing receipts without scheduling authors. Reject run-ID reuse unless an explicit recovery contract verifies it.
