findings.title: Farm gate retry loses containment failure
findings.implication: The executor distinguishes timeout with verified cleanup (124) from unverified cleanup (125/cleanupFailed). runGate reduces all nonzero outcomes to ordinary gate failure, allowing outer author reset/retry; mutation path treats unverified containment as fatal.
findings.recommendation: Return operation result, cancellation reason and containment status as separate typed fields through every caller. Block mutation/reset/retry until prior containment is verified, reusing the mutation path policy where applicable.
findings.domain: Pi, farm, sandbox, site and packaging

findings.title: Farm Git observation failure can appear as no drift
findings.implication: Failed diff/ls-files observations are replaced with empty arrays. Both failures can yield a clean-looking drift result.
findings.recommendation: Use observed-clean/observed-dirty/unavailable states; retry bounded read-only Git probes if appropriate, and stop effects when absence cannot be established.
findings.domain: Pi, farm, sandbox, site and packaging

findings.title: Sandbox dependency cache identity is tied to random checkout basename
findings.implication: Two creates with identical dependency files compute the same hash but random temporary checkout names produce different Docker tags, defeating intended cross-create cache reuse. Current caller also omits the available Nixpacks version component.
findings.recommendation: Build a stable cache key from dependency inputs, supported platform and actual builder/toolchain version. Keep repository name only as a cosmetic label; verify existing image provenance before reuse.
findings.domain: Pi, farm, sandbox, site and packaging

findings.title: Sandbox output overflow kills observation client without stopping workload
findings.implication: Overflow is returned as ordinary exit 1 rather than a distinct interrupted reason. exec stops container only for timeout/abort; probe observed no stop after overflow.
findings.recommendation: Carry overflow as explicit interrupted outcome and run the same verified containment policy as other lost-observation paths. Report stop outcome independently from command failure.
findings.domain: Pi, farm, sandbox, site and packaging

findings.title: Sandbox cleanup and discovery sometimes claim more than observed
findings.implication: Claude-inside error says destroyed after an ignored rm result that may be pre-aborted; create compensation ignores remove results; registry view returns [] when Docker listing fails. destroy/prune already contains a better explicit unknown/re-observe pattern.
findings.recommendation: Reuse destroy/prune observation contracts for create/Claude compensation and registry UI. Keep resource IDs and cleanup unknown until an un-aborted read confirms absence. Propagate cancellation through clone/build and bound helper cleanup.
findings.domain: Pi, farm, sandbox, site and packaging

findings.title: Site search handles loader failure but not query/result-data failure
findings.implication: Pagefind module import has retry state; search/data promises do not. Rejection can preserve stale current-looking results or disable show-all indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Give query and expansion their own error/retry state and finally cleanup, bound to the existing query generation token; retain input and clearly mark old results stale.
findings.domain: Pi, farm, sandbox, site and packaging

findings.title: Private Pi artifact prompt is not general installed Pi approval support
evidence: tools/build-host-packages.py:cold execution synthetic Pi approval evidence
findings.implication: Private entry requires exact Pi 1.0.2 while supported runtime compatibility is 1.1.0. It rejects ordinary agent flows; cold-package workflow reports synthetic-policy-event evidence for Pi. This cannot support a broad claim that all installed Pi artifact approvals are host-observed.
findings.recommendation: Publish a host/capability/evidence-mode matrix from actual admission contracts. Version private approval separately and qualify it on supported Pi before describing it as usable authority; preserve ordinary progress independent of optional attestation.
findings.domain: Pi, farm, sandbox, site and packaging

sources.symbol: cold execution synthetic Pi approval evidence

findings.title: Surface and release build helpers have recoverable partial-write states
findings.implication: Canonical generation is deterministic but many multi-file writes are not atomic; some remove old output before late render/rename failures. This is acceptable only if callers treat failed builds as unusable and rerun from canonical input.
findings.recommendation: Build into a complete fresh staging tree, validate there, then swap an owned output root where practical. Do not expand ordinary file tools into a distributed saga; apply durable receipts primarily to irreversible/external effects.
findings.domain: Pi, farm, sandbox, site and packaging

findings.title: Compatibility metadata validates a removal slogan, not release-history authorization
findings.implication: The literal removalRequires value is shape-checked during surface generation. It does not enforce elapsed releases, version floors, release publication status or actual command removal.
findings.recommendation: Keep provenance-aware removal gate separate and authoritative; generate compatibility prose from that enforceable contract instead of implying this registry literal proves removal eligibility.
findings.domain: Pi, farm, sandbox, site and packaging

findings.title: Claude and Codex promotion intentionally differ but share unknown-outcome recovery
findings.implication: Both pin immutable distribution commits, refuse same-version drift, lease channel writes and read back. Codex requires prior immutable tag before channel advance and rejects malformed current version; Claude combines tag/channel flow and skips downgrade comparison if prior version cannot be read.
findings.recommendation: Preserve host distribution differences. Share verified-ref outcome types and explicitly reject unknown current-channel version if monotonicity is required; provide fresh-work re-observation after any uncertain push rather than blind retry.
findings.domain: Pi, farm, sandbox, site and packaging

findings.title: Site drawer reconnect cleanup may duplicate local handlers
findings.implication: Cleanup removes document Escape handler and resets initialized marker but does not remove local opener/close/tray handlers; reconnecting the same element can bind duplicate toggles.
findings.recommendation: Own all listeners with one AbortController per connection, or retain the once-bound marker while reattaching document listeners. Add one connect-disconnect-reconnect behavior check only if this lifecycle is supported.
findings.confidence: source-confirmed; browser reconnect behavior not executed
findings.domain: Pi, farm, sandbox, site and packaging
findings.status: source-confirmed; browser reconnect behavior not executed
pure local decision probe reproduced; remote interruption not executed
findings.title: A public Release missing its final receipt cannot enter the advertised rerun recovery path
findings.claim: The composite publishes and reads back the Release before attaching codearbiter-publication.json. If that upload fails, plan() still reports a missing receipt, but eligible() rejects the already-public release. Both preflight and per-job recheck use eligible(), so retry skips the necessary remaining effect.
findings.probe: audit-work/probe_release_recovery_results.json: existing exact tag + public release + zero assets yields eligible=false while plan.missing-assets=codearbiter-publication.json
findings.recommendation: Make eligibility depend on verified target completion, or place the required receipt before the public transition. Preserve immutable tags/assets and allow only observed missing effects on retry.
findings.ux_dx_ax: Users can distinguish fully published from incomplete; maintainers get a working rerun; agents receive a precise resumable next action instead of contradictory eligible/plan results.

findings.title: Manual release description promises current main while source selection chooses latest successful main CI
findings.claim: The workflow accepts the latest successful main-push CI source if it is an ancestor of origin/main; it does not require equality to current main. This can be the correct artifact-bound recovery policy, but the UI/comment contract is different.
findings.recommendation: Show the exact selected CI run and source SHA in the manual action/result. Document latest successful main CI as the default or explicitly require current-head equality if owner policy demands it; do not silently change recovery semantics.

findings.title: Release-skill pre-tag proof is effectively a required gate despite ADR 40 retaining it as advisory
findings.claim: release.yml warns on declared pre-tag failure, but the required auto-release-candidate CI job invokes --run-pre-tag and raises on nonzero. ci-passed explicitly requires this job success. ADR 44 supersedes ADR 40 only for Pi npm signatures/attestation, leaving other advisory checks in force.
findings.recommendation: Obtain a governed policy decision on whether pre-tag proof is required, then encode the enforcement class once and derive both CI and publication behavior. Do not loosen a current required gate merely to make prose agree.

findings.title: Route compatibility publication clock has an implementation but no current release-workflow observation call
findings.claim: The checker implements planned/tag-only/draft/published/api-unavailable/mismatch and an API lookup, but current CI uses declarations/tests and neither release.yml nor publish-target calls observe/api-lookup. The CI comment assigning the post-publication audit to release.yml is not borne out by its contents. compatibility.removalRequires is not read by this checker.
findings.recommendation: Wire explicit non-mutating publication observation and retain its evidence if the compatibility clock is a real policy dependency; publish the declaration-only state until then. Keep removal policy adjudication separate from a field that is merely stored.

findings.title: Dedicated docs voice gate does not select PRs changing only its two rule implementation files
findings.claim: docs.yml includes .github/scripts/check_site_voice.py and core/pysrc/_sloplib.py under push paths but omits both under pull_request paths. The explanatory comment claims rule edits select the gate. Other CI tests may cover the rules, but this dedicated current-site voice run is not selected by those PR-only edits.
findings.recommendation: Generate or share the trigger input set for this gate, preserving deliberate event differences while adding its own implementation inputs to the PR selection contract.

findings.title: A successful exit sometimes means unavailable or optional skip, not verified protection/runtime
findings.claim: Ordinary tag audit permits unavailable API/no token; branch protection audit permits unknown fields without definite violation; optional Codex host check permits missing runtime. These are intentional branches but green status alone erases the evidence distinction for consumers.
findings.recommendation: Preserve existing exit compatibility while exposing a shared typed verdict such as verified, skipped, unavailable, rejected, including reasons and applicable scope. Let each gate declare which verdicts it accepts.

findings.status: source-confirmed branch conflation, no current base defect asserted
findings.title: Payload first-introduction classification conflates absent base manifest and invalid base version
findings.claim: base_version returns None for failed git show and for JSON/missing/non-string version. gate interprets every None as first introduction and returns success once current version is valid. Resolving the base commit first does not distinguish a present malformed manifest from an absent one.
findings.recommendation: Use distinct absent, valid and invalid read outcomes. Keep genuine new-plugin admission but reject invalid base evidence with a precise diagnostic.

findings.title: Two verification subprocess paths lack a bounded wait before their normal timeout path
findings.claim: Codex host _run has no timeout for marketplace/install/list commands. Pi production benchmark blocks in stdout.readline before communicate(timeout=30), so a child that never emits its first line can wait without that 30-second bound. No observed hang is asserted.
findings.recommendation: Make pending execution an explicit deadline/cancel outcome, preserving partial diagnostics and cleanup; characterize child-process termination requirements before changing process handling.

findings.status: source-confirmed and pure source-function probe; no actual unpublished production tag alleged
findings.title: Documentation derives published-release state from tag presence alone
findings.detail: selectCurrentGovernanceReleases chooses the highest stable local tag, accepts an empty original-publication receipt ledger, and labels its commit publicationCommit. Historical manifest equality and Pi-source parsing validate content identity but do not observe GitHub Release draft/published status. The publication workflow can create a tag before publishing. Therefore tag-only/draft and published states collapse at this site boundary.
findings.probe: probe-site-publication-result.json: synthetic stable tags and zero receipts are selected; no GitHub/network operation was performed.
findings.recommendation: Feed a durable observed non-draft publication record into site selection, keyed to immutable tag and payload identity. If that observation is unavailable, label a tag as a tag and leave publication unknown. Do not restore a stale receipt ledger as a blanket new-release gate.

findings.title: Statusline benchmark comparison can print PASS for zero measurements
findings.claim: cmd_compare iterates base.scenarios and accepts an empty object with no failures. cmd_run can naturally produce that empty object when every --scenario value is unknown, because it filters without validating the requested names.
findings.probe: audit-work/probe_tool_verdicts.json: empty base/head scenarios -> exit 0 and PASS text; no renderer ran.
findings.recommendation: Require a nonempty declared scenario population and compatible harness/measurement identity before any success verdict. Keep explicitly selected subsets visible rather than claiming full benchmark coverage.

findings.status: pure local oracle probe reproduced; subprocess-result issue source-confirmed
findings.title: Live SMARTS exercise tests literal lens-name presence rather than its stated material-comparison contract
findings.claim: The material judge accepts any three lens-name substrings in SEC-SMARTS. One paragraph containing Scalable Maintainable Available passed with no alternatives or table. main records judge output regardless of Claude return code, so a failed session can still produce PASS if its remaining spec satisfies this weak shape.
findings.probe: audit-work/probe_tool_verdicts.json: three lens names, one paragraph, table=false -> judge=true; no provider call ran.
findings.recommendation: Gate process completion separately from artifact validity, and validate explicit material alternatives/comparison semantics through native schema/contract checks plus bounded reviewed qualitative evidence. Do not equate substring count with a comparison.

findings.status: source-confirmed; no live baseline mismatch asserted
findings.title: CI20 evidence binds HEAD and current workflow hash without ensuring workflow bytes belong to that HEAD
findings.claim: collect checks run.head_sha == checkout HEAD, then parses the working-tree workflow. Neither baseline nor inventory requires clean tracked bytes or equality to git show HEAD:.github/workflows/ci.yml. A modified checkout can therefore label its analysis with a matching source commit while analyzing different workflow bytes.
findings.recommendation: Read workflow bytes from the bound commit or require exact blob equality before mapping jobs/commands. Preserve the observed file hash, run identity and counterfactual-vs-live distinction.

findings.title: Statusline illustration can proceed after failed renders and leaves some temporary inputs behind
findings.claim: Both statusline subprocess results are accepted without return-code/stderr validation. Normal cleanup omits earlier.jsonl and only removes legacy ledger.json, so the final directory removal can fail and is ignored. No screenshot corruption was reproduced in this audit.
findings.recommendation: Require successful nonempty render output before screenshotting, wrap all temporary state/browser lifetime in cleanup, and retain the image’s explicit mock-data provenance.

findings.title: Prune nudge threshold describes total context instead of freed context
findings.description: Configuration table says CODEARBITER_PRUNE_NUDGE_MIN_TOKENS sets minimum model-context size. Current nudge_decision compares estimated tokens from rec.context_bytes_freed to threshold. No runtime behavior change is recommended for this documentation correction.
findings.recommendation: Describe freed avoidable context accurately and derive this predicate/default from an executable contract instead of maintaining a second semantic description.

findings.classification: confirmed extractor limitation and overbroad generated claim
findings.title: Hook reference is a bounded static extraction, not all actual runtime message text
findings.description: Generated intro says it can never drift from what a hook prints. scanMessage drops variable/helper message suffixes, variable tag resolution is limited to30 lines, and skipped calls are not extracted. Current _bashguardlib security blocks append dynamic recovery strings. Literal-tag pass also omits codeMask test, so quoted/commented examples can be extracted as real calls; this latter false-positive possibility is static, not a demonstrated current site occurrence.
findings.recommendation: Label static templates/omitted dynamic pieces and display extraction gaps; use a typed gate registry or robust AST extraction for canonical IDs/events/recovery while keeping actual runtime code authoritative.
findings.status: confirmed extractor limitation and overbroad generated claim

findings.classification: static helper edge case, current production reachability not demonstrated
findings.title: Slug suffix counts do not reserve all output slugs
findings.description: assignSlugs tracks each base independently. The input sequence foo,foo,foo-2 produces foo,foo-2,foo-2 by direct control-flow inspection. Current installed-source names were not evaluated for such a collision in this supplemental read.
findings.recommendation: If arbitrary names remain supported, reserve emitted slugs globally and fail or consistently disambiguate collisions. Preserve previously published URL redirects when changing assignment.
findings.status: static helper edge case, current production reachability not demonstrated

findings.title: Sandbox preflight instructions refuse a dependency configuration that README and driver support
findings.claim: sandbox.md and lifecycle hard rules require nixpacks on PATH and STOP if absent. README explicitly allows Node/Python Dockerfile fallback, matching audited S49 fallback behavior. Following the installed workflow can unnecessarily block a supported create.
findings.recommendation: Derive host prerequisites and supported fallback coverage from one driver capability contract. Preserve a hard failure for unsupported stacks; do not require nixpacks when the selected stack has a verified fallback.

findings.status: direct contradiction between fully read command and skill
findings.title: The same shell exit means persistent box in one owner and teardown in another
findings.claim: sandbox-shell explicitly leaves the box running after shell exit until sandbox-destroy. lifecycle Phase 5 and hard rules trigger teardown when the interactive session closes. An agent following both has no unambiguous next action and could delete work the shell command said would persist.
findings.recommendation: Define shell detach versus sandbox destruction as separate events in one lifecycle owner. Preserve current runtime behavior until an intentional lifetime decision is approved; do not add automatic destructive teardown as a documentation cleanup.

findings.status: instruction scope conflict with audited target-aware cleanup
findings.title: Single-box destroy prose drifts into a global prune and global-empty postcondition
findings.claim: The destroy command accepts an explicit box ID but its flow then says prune remaining labeled objects and its hard gate demands zero plugin-labeled containers/volumes. Audited S53 deliberately freezes selected targets and does not retroactively treat unrelated/new resources as failure. Label ownership is broader than the operation’s selected instance.

sources.symbol: targeted destroy and explicit prune; S53

findings.recommendation: Specify a frozen operation target set. A named destroy verifies that instance; explicit prune/no-ID selects the broad labeled set. Report other active boxes separately and never broaden cleanup merely to satisfy global-empty wording.

findings.status: public storage claim contradicted by audited host staging
findings.title: Sandbox docs omit the temporary host copy of cloned source
findings.claim: sandbox.md and lifecycle say cloned code is never on the host filesystem; README says the cloned repo lives inside the container. Audited S48 create copies the checkout from the source volume into a newly named host temp directory for build analysis, then removes it in finally. This contradicts storage-location wording; it does not by itself show that the runtime container has a host bind mount.
findings.recommendation: State runtime mount isolation separately from host-side build staging, including temp location/lifetime/cleanup observations. Keep the no-bind/socket/privileged invariants; do not claim zero host source bytes while staging is implemented.

findings.status: advertised transition unavailable in current ordinary runtime
findings.title: Ordinary sandbox allowlist selection is described as applied although its run path stays offline
findings.claim: Command/skill/README offer ordinary allowlist policy and lifecycle Phase 3 says richer policies are applied by network.ts. Audited S50 finds NETWORKED_POLICIES empty and all ordinary runtime containers use --network none. The standalone helper and separate Claude-inside firewall path do not establish ordinary CLI integration.
findings.recommendation: Expose effective policy and current availability in generated help/instructions. Preserve offline behavior; any new network capability requires its own concrete implementation/verification and policy review.

findings.status: additional affected documentation for existing runtime finding SF08
findings.title: Cache reuse promise is repeated across independent sandbox surfaces
findings.claim: COMMANDS glossary, README, create command and lifecycle all promise identical dependency inputs imply identical tag/cache hit. Existing SF08/S49 identifies random create checkout basenames in the actual tag, defeating that cross-create promise.
findings.related_finding: SF08; no additional runtime defect is asserted
findings.recommendation: Correct stable cache identity once in the driver, then derive the same bounded reuse claim for every surface. Keep cache-hit proof separate from hash equality.

findings.title: Claude-inside requires codeArbiter maintainer evidence under the consumer project root
findings.claim: Preflight says read or STOP for two specific sandbox spike documents and ADR 0007 at CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.codearbiter. There is no packaged-reference fallback in the skill. Therefore a consumer project without those files is directed to stop even when driver/platform requirements are otherwise satisfied; the audit does not assume a particular user project’s files.
findings.recommendation: Ship a concise current prerequisite/capability contract at a plugin-owned path and cite maintainer evidence as commit-bound provenance. Do not require consumers to manufacture/copy internal ADR or historical spike files.

findings.status: prose enforcement claim exceeds executable admission
findings.title: Separate executable placement does not enforce five Claude-inside workflow phases
findings.claim: The skill says separate binary placement IS the gate and calls the five BLOCK phases enforced rather than advice. Fully read runClaudeInsideCli accepts image/home/policy, checks environment token presence, then calls runClaudeInside; it consumes no proof of caller identity, approved store, reviewed image or phase completion. Actual token-argv/source-volume/policy and runtime isolation guards remain real and should be credited individually.
findings.recommendation: Label model-guided checks and mechanically enforced guards accurately. Keep the separate supported entrypoint and real isolation checks; introduce no new mandatory proof/approval mechanism unless a concrete authority design is intentionally approved.

findings.status: README claims compared with fully audited hook owner evidence
findings.title: Claude README overstates dormant behavior and confines repository writes too narrowly
findings.claim: README says hooks immediately do nothing without .codearbiter and repository writes are .codearbiter only. The hook owner confirms session-start.main clears its mode marker and may heal globally owned statusline settings before the active-repository check. Opted-in initialization also installs Git hooks and writes selected Git-common info/exclude and hook bookkeeping outside .codearbiter. These are different scopes and should be stated separately.
findings.recommendation: Document repository enforcement activation separately from host-wide startup maintenance. List Git metadata writes and existing opt-in boundaries. This requires claim correction, not removing useful maintenance or broadening authority.

adr_assessments.assessment: Direction supports explicit state/evidence separation and ordinary progress without permission ceremony. It does not prohibit a compile-time transition registry. Existing strict optional paths must not become the default again. Task-block/STale and SMARTS resets need explicit semantic review against this principle.

Keep small kind-neutral file/CAS/journal kernel and closed per-kind contracts. Do not interpret accepted architecture as proof of implementation or a requirement for one mega state machine. It explicitly permits splitting proven boundaries if generic machinery harms correctness.

Supports staged intent, explicit sync, uncertainty reconciliation, no remote rollback claim. Manual Project sync-now is an explicit approved exception to issue after_merge timing; do not mistakenly homogenize it. Mapped effects add their own frozen generation/timing guards.
Historical campaign scope exception is not a permanent ban on locking/CAS; current native engine already has both. Do not cite it to reject common race hardening now.

Database-free remains consistent. Literal "no schema layer", "file-based prose", and "no transactional guarantees beyond append-only files" are superseded by implemented typed schema, HTML and journaled multi-file transactions plus ADR-0037. Do not add a database merely to model states; update historical/active claim classification.

adr_assessments.status: accepted in source; implementation compared rather than presumed
adr_assessments.supported: Independent per-target jobs, immutable existing-tag check, exact asset readback and dormant Codex npm helpers are implemented.
adr_assessments.conflicts: Its universal rerun recovery claim has C-F01 counterexample. Its release-skill pre-tag advisory policy conflicts with required CI in C-F03.
adr_assessments.decision: Keep independent target publication and immutable artifact rules. Define a per-target completion predicate and govern the enforcement-class inconsistency; do not reintroduce cross-target cohort locking.

Decision: Keep independent target publication and immutable artifact rules. Define a per-target completion predicate and govern the enforcement-class inconsistency; do not reintroduce cross-target cohort locking.

adr_assessments.status: accepted in source; live npm account configuration not observed
adr_assessments.supported: Active publish command uses OIDC provenance and no static token fallback; exact integrity, signatures and repo/workflow/source attestation gate finishing GitHub release, including recovery of existing versions.
adr_assessments.limits: Source inspection cannot verify npm trusted-publisher account configuration or an actual successful release. ADR explicitly requires live qualification.
adr_assessments.decision: Retain fail-closed identity gate and pending-draft recovery; expose pending registry/attestation states with their deadline and next action.

Limits: Source inspection cannot verify npm trusted-publisher account configuration or an actual successful release. ADR explicitly requires live qualification. Decision: Retain fail-closed identity gate and pending-draft recovery; expose pending registry/attestation states with their deadline and next action.

Its per-session-and-mode cache description conflicts with its promise of injection on each mode change. The reproduced A→B→A sequence suppresses the return injection. Bind delivery to current selection/generation/content and amend the cache contract; do not treat the accepted text as proof that transitions work.

Retain bounded authorization and actual host/user hard stops. Explicit state contracts can carry existing authority without new approval ceremonies. Any removal of a current confirmation or change in authority semantics is a distinct reviewable decision.

The ordinary CI candidate path makes a nominally advisory pre-tag command a gate, and published-without-receipt is not admitted by the outer recovery eligibility path. Reconcile those facts with the ADR rather than claiming its rerun/advisory intent is implemented.
This decision changes Pi publication trust/provenance. It does not by itself supersede the unrelated pre-tag advisory rule or repair the published-release receipt recovery admission gap.

coverage.overview: The audit inventories the entire pinned Git tree and reads the primary implementation/workflow owners. Full text, complete executable content, targeted reads, byte-verified shared copies and renderer-verified derivatives are distinguished per file. Historical reports, most tests, fixtures, static assets and external dependency internals are not misrepresented as independently audited current implementations.

equivalence_checks.build_surface_check: PASS; claude/codex/pi in sync; no source files written

coverage.definition: A machine is retained lifecycle/operation state, asynchronous ownership, transaction/recovery state, contextual parser state, or a model-guided workflow that changes allowed next events or observable effects. Pure formatting helpers and explicit teaching diagrams are classified under their owner rather than counted as independent product lifecycles. The table covers identified transitions; it is not a formal proof that every possible interleaving or environment failure has been enumerated.
scope_limits: No installed or distributed package was qualified by this source audit. Tracked bundled JavaScript and native binaries were inventoried; their complete source equivalence was not independently rebuilt here.
Most test files and historical audit/design records were inventoried rather than read in full. Targeted tests and probes are explicitly listed; earlier audits are not treated as current proof.
Imported third-party runtime internals (including host implementations and Astro/Starlight controls) were not inferred or independently audited. Repo-owned integration state is included.
This is only arbiterForge/codeArbiter. Other organization repositories, separate public websites and Academy release artifacts were not audited or changed.
Read-only source inspection plus bounded fixtures; no Go runtime, real Docker/provider farm, real host GUI, remote publication or external issue/Project mutation.
coverage.project_sources: Operating contract and relevant portfolio/claim policy were inspected. Older portfolio/claim facts were commit-bound context and were not substituted for live GitHub. Proposed deltas are in the report; no Project Sources were edited.
